title: Haptic perception
limitations: Review article with no original empirical data
No statistical tests performed by authors

key_concepts: Material properties perception (roughness, compliance, coldness, friction, viscosity, density, weight)
Spatial properties perception (shape, curvature, length, volume, orientation)
Haptic illusions (geometric optical illusions in touch, thermal illusions, curvature after-effects, location illusion)
Applications (haptic devices, robotic feedback, teleoperation, virtual reality)
major_sections: Material Properties: roughness, compliance, coldness, friction, viscosity, density/weight
Spatial Properties: shape, curvature, length, volume, orientation
fundamental_claims: Humans can perceive material properties through active touch using stereotypical movement patterns called exploratory procedures
Haptic perception operates through cutaneous (skin) and proprioceptive (joint/muscle) information
Perception of haptic properties depends on reference frames (egocentric, allocentric, hand-centered) and exploratory strategy
Haptic and visual perception are largely independent but can interact through multimodal integration
Haptic information is essential for applications like teleoperation, remote surgery, robotics, and virtual reality interfaces

content_summary.abstract: This overview paper surveys the state of the art in haptic perception research. It covers both material properties (roughness, compliance, friction, coldness, viscosity, density/weight) and spatial properties (shape, curvature, length, volume, orientation) that humans can perceive through touch. The paper discusses exploratory procedures, discrimination thresholds, and the role of reference frames in haptic perception. It also covers haptic illusions (geometric optical illusions, thermal illusions, curvature after-effects, location illusions) and applications of haptic knowledge to technology (haptic devices, robotic feedback, teleoperation, virtual reality).
content_summary.paper_type: Narrative review of haptic perception literature

notes: This is a review article, not an original research study
Contains extensive references to cited studies but no original data collection or statistical analysis
Comprehensive coverage of haptic perception domains suitable for establishing foundational knowledge
Contains numerous figures illustrating exploratory procedures and perceptual tasks
